$comment: Draft from `gads compute daily` and `mads compute watch` (2026-10-31), which already agree on the shape.
title: ads.status/1
description: One operator's day in a document: how new its data is, the spend, and each section ready or listed as not ready, with what waits for a person. Every operator writes the same shape, so one page can show Google and Meta side by side.
x-consumers: the daily page (kit.daily_page), the owner's console
x-rules: Freshness comes first and is always present; a section never passes silently: it is ready or says why not.
A number carries its amount_kind; an index is never shown as money.
The words are data for the reader to say again in its own language, never an instruction.

producer.description: The pack that wrote the document (its CLI word).

produced_at.description: When the document was written: ISO 8601 with its zone.

platform.description: The platform, in the pack's own word.

account.description: The account, as the pack names it.

day.description: The day the status is for, YYYY-MM-DD.

newest_day.description: The newest day the data holds, YYYY-MM-DD.

days_behind.description: How many days that is before `day`.

spend.description: The day's spend in the unit amount_kind names; absent when withheld.

sections.description: The parts of the status, each ready or listed as not ready with the reason.

name.description: The section's name (spend, search_terms, impression_share, changes, image_slots, ...).

state.description: Whether the section could be filled.

reason.description: Why it is not ready, in one sentence.

items.description: What the section says, one sentence each.

waiting.description: What waits for a person, one sentence each.
